signals.evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/migration.rs:678-798 upload_import_file (POST /api/v1/migration/import/upload, wired at routes/migration.rs:59 and lib.rs:320) is a silent stub that drops the uploaded file bytes. At line 693 it declares `let mut _file_data: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();` (the leading underscore is the Rust 'intentionally unused' marker that suppresses the dead-store warning). At line 715-720 it reads the full multipart body into memory with `field.bytes().await` and assigns it to `_file_data = data.to_vec();`. That buffer is never used again anywhere in the file (grep for `_file_data` returns only these two lines). At line 757 it fabricates a storage path `let file_path = format!("imports/{}/{}", org_id, Uuid::new_v4());` with NO call to any S3/MinIO/filesystem writer, then at line 764-779 passes that non-existent path to `migration_repo.create_import_job(...)` and returns 200 with job_id + 'File uploaded successfully. Validation will begin shortly.' (line 796). Impact: (a) data loss — platform admins who upload a bulk-import file (buildings/units/residents/financial records, up to 100 MB per MAX_IMPORT_SIZE at line 734) receive a success response and a job_id but no file was ever persisted; (b) silent broken feature — downstream processing (`get_import_job_status`, `validate_import`, `approve_import`) references a `file_path` that resolves to nothing; (c) memory bloat — the handler still allocates up to 100 MB into a Vec<u8> per concurrent request before dropping it. Reachability: router nested at lib.rs:320 under `/api/v1/migration`, mod declared at routes/mod.rs:101 `pub mod migration;`. Confidence HIGH: the `_file_data` dead-store and the lack of any writer call are directly observable; the fabricated file_path pattern and the `Pending` status at line 770 confirm the stub intent. Severity HIGH (+3): data-loss class on a platform-admin migration endpoint whose entire purpose is to persist tenant data, not a mere I/O bug. Fix: route the uploaded bytes through `state.storage_service` (same pattern as other upload sites, e.g. documents) BEFORE creating the import job, use the actual storage key as `file_path`, and reject the request if `storage_service` is not configured (fail-closed) instead of returning success.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/migration.rs:1241-1398 — the migration export flow (POST /api/v1/migration/export → GET /api/v1/migration/export/{id} → GET /api/v1/migration/export/{id}/download) is a stub that fabricates its outputs. In `get_export_status` the explicit comment at line 1268 says `// Auto-transition to Ready in mock setup`, and lines 1269-1291 unconditionally flip the record from Pending to Ready, writing a hardcoded placeholder file_path `let path = format!("https://storage.example.com/exports/{}.zip", export_id);` (line 1270), a hardcoded fake file_size_bytes `Some(15_234_567)` (line 1278), and a fabricated completed_at `Some(chrono::Utc::now())` (line 1283). No real export job has run — `request_migration_export` (lines 1183-1239) only inserts a DB row, there is no backing worker or writer that materialises the archive. Then at lines 1312-1316 the response hands the admin a hardcoded fake record_counts payload `{ "buildings": 45, "units": 320, "residents": 580 }` regardless of the org's actual data. Finally `download_export` (line 1393-1395) returns `download_url: updated.file_path.unwrap_or_else(|| format!("https://storage.example.com/exports/{}.zip", export_id))` — the admin UI gets a `storage.example.com` URL (an IANA reserved illustration domain, RFC 2606, that will never resolve to real content). Reachability: router nested at lib.rs:320, `pub mod migration;` at routes/mod.rs:101, routes wired at routes/migration.rs:66-69. Impact: silent broken feature — platform admins requesting a migration export see 'Ready' with a plausible file size and record counts, but every download URL is a dead `storage.example.com` link and no archive exists. This is distinct from the already-flagged `code-review-api-handlers-data-export-report-stub` / `code-review-api-handlers-report-dl-deadlink` findings (different modules: reports/mod.rs vs. migration.rs) and from `multi-currency-refresh-stub-success` (different domain). Confidence HIGH: the hardcoded example.com URL, the fabricated record counts, and the 'mock setup' author comment at line 1268 are direct quotes from the source. Severity MEDIUM (+2): platform-admin-only, no data loss, but a silently broken customer-visible feature on a flagship Epic 66.3 migration-export surface, with user-trust and compliance impact (admin thinks data was exported). Fix: either (a) hide the endpoints behind a feature flag until a real exporter lands, or (b) implement the backing export job and persist a real presigned URL from the storage service in the file_path column, and drop the hardcoded `storage.example.com` fallback at line 1395.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/admin/impersonation.rs:114 `list_active` reads the raw X-Forwarded-For header verbatim for audit logging: `let ip = headers.get("x-forwarded-for").and_then(|h| h.to_str().ok());`, then passes the full comma-separated chain to `audit.record(..., ip, ua)` at line 126. This bypasses the shared helper `audit_ip_from_headers` defined at routes/admin/mod.rs:60-75, which the sibling `start` handler in the SAME file uses correctly at line 195 (`let ip = super::audit_ip_from_headers(&headers);`). The helper's doc comment (admin/mod.rs:41-55) states it exists specifically to prevent silent audit-row drops: `audit_logs.ip_address` is VARCHAR(45) (admin/mod.rs:44 `AUDIT_IP_MAX_LEN: usize = 45`), and a typical multi-hop X-Forwarded-For chain (e.g. `203.0.113.7, 198.51.100.1, 10.0.0.1` = 36 chars; three IPv6 hops easily exceed 45) overflows the column. Impact: when the audit INSERT fails on an overlong IP string, the handler's error branch at line 130-132 only emits `tracing::warn!(error = %e, "audit write for impersonation/active failed")` and returns 200 OK with the full cross-tenant impersonation list — so the compliance-mandated audit trail of 'who viewed the active-impersonation dashboard' silently has gaps for any viewer behind >1 proxy. Divergence is clear within the file itself: `start` (line 195), `stop` (not applicable — no audit call), and every audit site in sibling admin/* files use `audit_ip_from_headers`. Reachability: `GET /api/v1/admin/impersonation/active` is wired via lib.rs:145 (`admin::router()`) → admin/mod.rs:94 (`impersonation::router()`) → impersonation.rs:28 (`.route("/active", get(list_active)...)`). This is DISTINCT from the prior finding `code-review-api-handlers-share-log-proxy-ip` which is about `documents/shares.rs` share access logs, not admin impersonation. Confidence HIGH: the raw-XFF read, the helper's existence, and the sibling `start` call-site all read directly from the file. Severity MEDIUM (+2): compliance/audit-trail integrity on a platform-admin impersonation surface — an attacker-controlled or merely multi-proxy X-Forwarded-For value silently drops the 'who viewed active impersonations' audit row. No crash, no data loss, no auth bypass. Fix: replace line 114 with `let ip = super::audit_ip_from_headers(&headers);` to mirror the `start` handler's call site.
